commits: c421fa6eb8d82562e30ad26c8c32ee99037d29a1 test: the roles All and Desk User grant no change to an accounting document
fixed.red: This was an unproven finding, and the missing check was about what the ERPNext image grants, not about Enterich's code. So I made the change a new image release could make, directly on the e2e site (scripts/erpnext-site.sh up, http://127.0.0.1:8080): as Administrator, through the role permission manager, I added a Desk User rule on Payment Request and gave it write. Then I ran `E2E_ERPNEXT_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080 uv run pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/e2e/test_ceiling.py -k desk_user`. It failed with `AssertionError: assert [('Payment Re...', ['write'])] == []` at `assert changing == []`. I reset Payment Request's rules with permission_manager.reset, which left no Custom DocPerm on it, ran the test again and it passed. On the unchanged site it passes as well. The non-e2e pytest run (1340 passed), ruff check, ruff format --check, basedpyright and mdformat --check all pass.
fixed.notes: The branch auto/security-e2e-ceiling did not exist yet, so I started from origin/main, and the branch now holds only this commit. The test reads, as Administrator, the rules of All and Desk User that are actually in force: a DocType's Custom DocPerm rules replace its DocPerm rules once it has any. It asserts that none of them grants create, write, submit, cancel, amend or delete on a submittable DocType, or on a DocType in the modules Accounts, Assets, Buying, Selling, Setup, Stock or Subcontracting. Today the only changing rules those roles hold are on Desk, Core, Contacts, Integrations and similar DocTypes. The test cites REQ-002-PRS-NF013 and the configuration guide's "Inherited rights" bullet. The e2e site was left running, and it is reusable.

review.reason:
The single commit c421fa6 (test:) changes only tests/e2e/test_ceiling.py, adding 44 lines at :181-224 on a branch started from origin/main (fd37c1b). It adds what the finding says is missing: a check of the configuration guide's "Inherited rights" bullet (docs/guides/configuration.md:66, REQ-002-PRS-NF013). The test reads the rules of All and Desk User that are in force, as Administrator. Custom DocPerm replaces DocPerm for each DocType that has any. It asserts that none of them grants create, write, submit, cancel, amend or delete on a submittable DocType or a DocType in an accounting module. That is the check the finding proposed, in the file its verdict named. No existing test checks this: test_ceiling.py checks only the four drafted DocTypes, and test_rights.py covers only its RIGHTS rows. The new test uses the existing Site.call and Site.get_list helpers and the site/seeded fixtures, as its neighbours do.

I redid the red check in a detached worktree at c421fa6 against the running e2e site (http://127.0.0.1:8080). On the unchanged site the test passed. I then applied the reported break through permission_manager.add/update: Desk User given write on Payment Request, plus All given create on Account, a non-submittable Accounts DocType. The test failed with "AssertionError: assert [('Payment Re..., ['create'])] == []" and two items listed. I reset both DocTypes with permission_manager.reset and it passed again. The reset on Account also removed the seeded Enterich Agent rule, so I reran tests/e2e/seed.seed, which is idempotent, to restore it. The first combined run of test_ceiling.py and test_rights.py right after that reseed had 101 failures. Each file then passed on its own (25 and 99), and a second combined run passed 124 of 124, so the failures were transient and not caused by the commit. ruff check, ruff format --check and basedpyright are clean on the file. Nothing outside the finding changed, and a test: commit needs no CHANGELOG line. I removed the worktree and the scratch scripts; the repository is unchanged.
